The gap was about 80 percentage points at its peak, not 40 or 50. In the mid-1950s, Southern approval of school desegregation was only about 14%, while approval in the rest of the U.S. was far higher. I'm picking the -80% option over -40%, but my recollection of the exact figures is shaky, so this is a judgment call.

CONFIDENCE: 40
